description.narrative:
The Jordanian National Commission for Women and the Ministry of Labour carried out a review of national laws and policies vis-à-vis Convention No. 190 and its accompanying Recommendation No. 206.
Following discussion and validation of the gaps analysis (December 2020), the document, including the recommendations for changes in laws and policies, was endorsed by the Jordanian National Commission for Women and by the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions. The document is now awaiting the final endorsement by the Ministry of Labour.
The proposed amendments to the labour law in relation to issues related to violence and harassment in the world of work were also included in a separate position paper, which was presented to the Prime Ministry and the Gender Inter-ministerial Committee. The position paper is currently being reviewed by the Parliament.
Following up on the finding of the gaps analysis, the Jordanian National Commission for Women and the General Federation of Trade Unions endorsed a draft national strategy to address violence and harassment, which lists the laws, tools, policies, procedures, and complaints mechanisms that need to be in place in line with C190. The draft national strategy is currently being reviewed by the Ministry of Labour and the Chamber of Industry and it is expected to be endorsed once the labour law is amended. The ILO has provided extensive support to constituents and other stakeholders, including civil society organisations, towards the development and validation of the review of laws and policies vis-à-vis C190. The ILO also supported the drafting of the position paper for its submission to the Prime Ministry and the Gender Inter-ministerial Committee. Support was also been provided for the development of a draft kit for employers and employees on how to prevent of and protect from violence and harassment at the workplace. The draft will be finalised once the labour law reform is finalised.
With a view to support effective changes and support constituents towards the effective implementation of the Convention, the ILO is also strengthening the capacity of Government's, employers' and workers' representatives through training programme, which is scheduled to take place in October and November 2021 in collaboration with ITC Turin.

description.narrative: The Jordanian National Commission for Women has revised the national framework on childcare to include accreditation to both workers in nurseries as well as employers in the sector. This will allow for increasing the value of the sector as well as professionalizing the jobs in the sector. With support of the SIDA, the ILO provided technical support to the Jordanian National Commission for Women in revising the national framework on childcare.

description.narrative: The Social Security Corporation has amended the social security law to permit the use of part of the reserves of the Maternity Insurance programme (the Social Security Fund from which maternity benefits are paid) to cover the costs of childcare for working mothers who had to return to work while schools remained closed as part of Covid-19 containment measures. The childcare subsidy is provided at a staggered rate – the lower the mother's income the higher the subsidy and operational cost subsidy at 50% for nurseries as this sector was also affected. With support of the SIDA, the ILO provided technical inputs to guide the Social Security Corporation in the amendment of the Social Security law and Regulation.
